draft.title: Coding and non-coding DNA
card: Coding DNA contains the instructions for making proteins. In humans, only a small part of the genome is coding DNA, roughly 1 to 2%.
Non-coding DNA does not code for a protein. It makes up most of the genome in humans.
Some non-coding regions control gene expression. They help decide when, where and how much a gene is switched on.

Two cells can hold the same genes but make different proteins, because different control regions are active in each cell type. A change in a control region can alter when a gene is used without changing the protein it codes for.
draft.remember: Coding DNA makes proteins. Some non-coding DNA controls when genes are switched on.

a.q: Which statement about non-coding DNA is correct?
opts: Some of it controls when genes are switched on
It is the part of DNA that is copied into proteins
It is found only in cells that do not make proteins
It makes up only a small part of the human genome
a.why: Some non-coding regions act as control regions for gene expression. Non-coding DNA is not a small part of the human genome: it is most of it, and the small part is the coding DNA.
a.clue: Think about what control regions do for a gene.

b.q: A muscle cell and a skin cell in the same person hold identical DNA, but they make different sets of proteins. Which explanation fits best?
opts: Different control regions are active in each cell type
The skin cell has lost the coding DNA for muscle proteins
Non-coding DNA is converted into protein in muscle cells
Muscle cells contain more coding DNA than skin cells
b.why: The cells share the same genes, but active control regions switch different genes on in each cell type. The idea that skin cells lost muscle genes is tempting, but both cells hold the same DNA.
b.clue: The cells hold the same DNA, so what differs is which genes are used.

a.best: Some of it controls when genes are switched on

b.best: Different control regions are active in each cell type

problems.detail: "Coding DNA makes proteins" is loose for Year 12. DNA does not make proteins: it carries the instructions (via mRNA). The card itself says it "contains the instructions for making proteins", so the remember line should match, e.g. "Coding DNA codes for proteins."
